member.remarks: A versioned item cannot be copied to another versioned item. For example, a processing method cannot be copied with the option to another sequence, but to another folder. member.name: M:Thermo.Chromeleon.Sdk.Interfaces.Data.IDataItem.Reload
member.summary: Discards the currently loaded data and child collections. This enforces reloading the data and children on next access.
member.remarks: The reload operation is recursive.

member.name: M:Thermo.Chromeleon.Sdk.Interfaces.Data.IDataItem.Delete
member.summary: Deletes the item from the datasource.

remarks.para: The item is marked as "Deleted". When the transaction is committed, the item is actually deleted from the datasource. When the transaction is rolled back, the "Deleted" flag is removed, and the item is not deleted.
A deleted item is removed from the child collection of the parent, and the Parent property returns null. Children of the deleted item are recursively marked as "deleted"
Deleting an item does not mean disposing the cache item. However, when an item is marked as "Deleted", all further write operations fail and raise an exception.

member.exception: The item is the recycle bin.

member.name: M:Thermo.Chromeleon.Sdk.Interfaces.Data.IInjection.ApplySequenceDefaults(Thermo.Chromeleon.Sdk.Interfaces.Data.ISequence)
member.summary: Applies the type definition (e.g. the valid ranges for the inject volume etc.) of the corresponding .

remarks.para: Please note this method won't modify the corresponding values. A call to this method could leave the injection in an invalid state (values violate the new type definitions). It's up to the caller to correct the values later on or use the corresponding overload .

It is mandatory that the injection doesn't belong to another sequence. This method could be useful if you want to move or copy an injection from one sequence to another and you expect type violations. Currently the SDK doesn't offer the option to modify the type of the corresponding values (e.g. with ) directly. So in order to modify the values of the injection to fit the new type definition of a target sequence the following steps should be done:
Unhook the injection from the current parent data item (e.g. sequence)
Call or to assign the new types (and values).
Correct the values of the injection in order to satisfy the new type definitions.
Assign the injection to the new sequence.

member.param: The sequence which type definitions should be applied.
member.exception: Throw the exception if the current instance already belongs to another .

member.name: M:Thermo.Chromeleon.Sdk.Interfaces.Data.IInjection.ApplySequenceDefaults(Thermo.Chromeleon.Sdk.Interfaces.Data.ISequence,System.Boolean)
member.summary: See . This overload offers the option to automatically modify the values in order to satisfy the new type definitions.
member.param: The sequence which type definitions should be applied.
if set to true the values will be modified in order to satisfy the new type definitions. If a value violates the new type definition, the default value of the new type definition will be applied.
member.exception: Throw the exception if the current instance already belongs to another .

member.name: M:Thermo.Chromeleon.Sdk.Interfaces.Data.IItemFactory.Flush
member.summary: Clears the cache from items that are not referenced by the application.
member.remarks: The method removes all strong references to items from the cache. It also sets the remaining cleanup counter for all item to 0. Then it calls the garbage collector and removes all dead weak item references. The method does not remove items of these types: RootItem, DataSourceHost, DataSource. However, it removes the child collection of the DataSource items. If any item (but RootItem, DataSourceHost, DataSource) survives this method call it can be expected that somewhere outside the item cache exists a strong references to the item.

member.summary: Creates an injection query based on two formula strings. The first one represent the quick search query part and the second one the computed query part. The quick search part will be used to create a SQL query internally. The computed query part will be used to filter the result of the quick part execution base on the Chromeleon report engine.
member.param: Indicates if the or strings are culture invariant.
member.remarks:
The two strings ( and ) are based on the well known Chromeleon report formula syntax. Currently there are some known limitation regarding the part:
LIKE/NOT LIKE operators are not supported
DURING PREVIOUS/NOT DURING PREVIOUS is not supported
DURING PREVIOUS/NOT DURING PREVIOUS is not supported

member.summary: The units that you can associate with mass tolerance. Taken from CommonCore.

member.name: F:Thermo.Chromeleon.Sdk.Interfaces.Data.MsToleranceUnits.Mmu
member.summary: Millimass units: a unit of mass equal to 0.001 atomic mass unit, used in physics and chemistry. This unit is also called the millidalton (mDa). The millimass unit is an SI unit, but its proper SI symbol is mu, not the older symbol mmu

member.name: F:Thermo.Chromeleon.Sdk.Interfaces.Data.MsToleranceUnits.Ppm
member.summary: Parts-per-million: a concentration, a unit of proportion equal to 10^-6.

member.name: F:Thermo.Chromeleon.Sdk.Interfaces.Data.MsToleranceUnits.Amu
member.summary: Atomic mass units: the unit of mass used by chemists and physicists for measuring the masses of atoms and molecules. Early in the nineteenth century, scientists discovered that each chemical element is composed of atoms, and that each chemical compound is composed of molecules in which atoms are combined in a fixed way. The definition of the unified atomic mass unit as 1/12 the mass of the most common atoms of carbon, known as carbon-12 atoms. (Most elements are mixtures of atoms which have different masses because they contain different numbers of neutrons; these varieties are called isotopes.) Careful experiments have measured the size of this unit; the currently accepted value (1998) is 1.660 538 73 x 10-24 grams. (This number equals 1 divided by Avogadro's number; see mole.) In addition, 1 amu equals approximately 931.494 MeV (see electron volt). In biochemistry, the atomic mass unit is called the dalton (Da).

the data cannot be set for any reason. Possible reasons:
A third party framework (i.e. Agilent ICF) required by the plug-in isn't installed on the client where the SDK is running. Solution: install the framework.

The SDK cannot map a legacy data block to a plug-in's driver id.

member.name: T:Thermo.Chromeleon.Sdk.Interfaces.Data.InstrumentMethodScript.IExpression
member.summary: A chromeleon script expression. A script expression is a mathematical expression that results in numeric or a string value.

remarks.para: The result type of the expression must fit to the property or parameter to which the resulting value will be assigned.
Example for a numeric expression: 'ColumnOven.Temperature.Nominal + 2.0 / 10.0' Example for a string expression: '"Column is connected to " + Column.PumpDevice'.

Expressions are also used as conditions in conditional steps. The result type of conditional expressions is always numeric. Zero values will be interpreted as 'false', all other values will be interpreted as 'true'.

An expression can contain constant values and/or references to other properties that are defined in the instrument's symbol tree. If an expression contains constant values only, it can be evaluated at any time. In this case either or (depending on the result type) returns a valid value. If the expression contains symbol references, its value can be evaluated at script run time only and or will always return a null value.

member.summary:
The instrument setup stage (initial) stage.
The time of this stage will be . This stage can not have a nominal duration greater than zero.

member.name: F:Thermo.Chromeleon.Sdk.Interfaces.Data.InstrumentMethodScript.SeparationMethodStage.Equilibration
member.summary:
This stage contains steps used for instrument equilibration before inject.
Typically pump equilibration will be done in this stage. This stage can contain time steps with negative times up to inject time.

member.name: F:Thermo.Chromeleon.Sdk.Interfaces.Data.InstrumentMethodScript.SeparationMethodStage.InjectPreparation
member.summary:
This stage contains steps that prepare the instrument for injection.
Typically, this stage contains a wait command that puts the instrument into 'Hold' mode until all devices are ready. This stage can not have a nominal duration greater than zero, which means all steps in this stage will be at inject time (time zero).

member.name: F:Thermo.Chromeleon.Sdk.Interfaces.Data.InstrumentMethodScript.SeparationMethodStage.Inject
member.summary:
This stage contains steps that performs an inject operation.
Typically, this stage contains the sampler's inject command. This stage can not have a nominal duration greater than zero, which means all steps in this stage will be at inject time (time zero).

member.name: F:Thermo.Chromeleon.Sdk.Interfaces.Data.InstrumentMethodScript.SeparationMethodStage.StartRun
member.summary:
This stage contains steps that are performed immediately after inject.
Typically, this stage contains Acquisition On command steps that start data acquisition for detector channels. This stage can not have a nominal duration greater than zero, which means all steps in this stage will be at inject time (time zero).

member.name: F:Thermo.Chromeleon.Sdk.Interfaces.Data.InstrumentMethodScript.SeparationMethodStage.Run
member.summary:
This stage contains steps that are performed during the method run at positive times.
This stage can have a duration grater than zero.

member.name: F:Thermo.Chromeleon.Sdk.Interfaces.Data.InstrumentMethodScript.SeparationMethodStage.StopRun
member.summary:
This stage contains steps that stop data acquisition and terminates a regular method run.
Typically, this stage contains Acquisition Off commands for detector channels. This stage can not have a nominal duration greater than zero.

member.name: F:Thermo.Chromeleon.Sdk.Interfaces.Data.InstrumentMethodScript.SeparationMethodStage.PostRun
member.summary:
This stage contains all steps that are performed after data acquisition.
Most time this stage isn't used in regular instrument methods.

member.summary:
Represents a stage in an instrument method .
A stage is a special part in an instrument method script and contains time steps . The first in a stage is the default time step which cannot be removed.

member.name: P:Thermo.Chromeleon.Sdk.Interfaces.Data.InstrumentMethodScript.IStage.Time
member.summary: The begin time of the stage.
member.remarks:
If the stage is the origin stage, its time cannot be changed. The origin stage is the 'Run' stage for scripts of type and the 'TimeTabledCommands' stage for scripts of type .
Changing the time of a stage past the origin stage will shift all successive stages to later times. Furthermore, its time can be changed only if the predecessor stage is a time table section ( is true).
Changing the time of a stage before the origin stage will shift all preceding stages to negative times. Furthermore, its time can be changed only if this stage is a time table section ( is true).

member.name: F:Thermo.Chromeleon.Sdk.Interfaces.Data.InstrumentMethodScript.StepType.If
member.summary:
An 'if' conditional step.
The 'If' step has always exactly one command parameter in its . This command parameter has the name 'Condition' and represents the condition expression of the if step. If the expression yields true, the child steps of this step will be processed.

member.name: F:Thermo.Chromeleon.Sdk.Interfaces.Data.InstrumentMethodScript.StepType.ElseIf
member.summary:
An 'Else If' conditional step.
The 'Else If' step has always exactly one command parameter in its . This command parameter has the name 'Condition' and represents the condition expression of the if step. If the expression yields true, the child steps of this step will be processed.

member.name: F:Thermo.Chromeleon.Sdk.Interfaces.Data.InstrumentMethodScript.StepType.Else
member.summary:
An 'Else' conditional step.
The child steps of this step will be processed if neither the step nor any of the steps have an expression that yields true.

member.name: F:Thermo.Chromeleon.Sdk.Interfaces.Data.InstrumentMethodScript.StepType.While
member.summary:
A 'While' conditional step.
The 'While' step has always exactly one command parameter in its . This command parameter has the name 'Condition' and represents the condition expression of if step. Child steps of this step will be processed if neither the 'If' nor any of the 'Else If' steps have an expression that yields true.

member.name: F:Thermo.Chromeleon.Sdk.Interfaces.Data.InstrumentMethodScript.StepType.Trigger
member.summary:
A trigger step.
A trigger has several parameters in its . Most important are parameters 'Name' and the 'Condition'.
The Name parameter defines the trigger name which must be unique in the script. The Condition parameter contains a condition expression.
The condition expression will be continuously evaluated during a method run. Every time the result of the condition expression changes from false (zero) to true (non-zero) the trigger execution block (the trigger's child steps) will be executed.
Other parameters control the trigger execution. For details, please refer to the Chromeleon help.

member.summary: The recorded spectrum with the given zero-based index.

member.returns: The recorded spectrum with the given zero-based index.

member.name: M:Thermo.Chromeleon.Sdk.Interfaces.Data.ISpectralField.IndexAtOrBefore(System.Double)
member.summary:
Return the zero-based index of the recorded spectrum at or before the given retention time. The time is increased by a small epsilon (currently 1E-12) before the search to avoid rounding problems with floating point numbers.
The native implementation uses a binary search. The time complexity of this function is in this case therefore O(log(Count)).
member.exception: If there are no retention times
If the retention time is less than the time of the first spectrum.
member.param: The retention time whose spectrum index is searched.
member.returns: A valid zero-based spectrum index.

member.name: M:Thermo.Chromeleon.Sdk.Interfaces.Data.ISpectralField.IndexAtOrAfter(System.Double)
member.summary:
Return the zero-based index of the recorded spectrum at or after the given retention time. The time is decreased by a small epsilon (currently 1E-12) before the search to avoid rounding problems with floating point numbers.
The native implementation uses a binary search. The time complexity of this function is in this case therefore O(log(Count)).
member.exception: If there are no retention times
If the retention time is greater than the time of the last spectrum.
member.param: The retention time whose spectrum index is searched.
member.returns: A valid zero-based spectrum index.

member.name: M:Thermo.Chromeleon.Sdk.Interfaces.Data.ISpectralField.InterpolateSpectrum(System.Double)
member.summary: Compute a linear interpolated spectrum at the given retention time. An exception will be thrown if the time is outside the time range of the spectral field. I.e. this function cannot be used to extrapolate a spectrum.
member.param: The retention time at which the interpolated spectrum should be computed.
member.returns: The linear interpolated spectrum at the requested retention time.

member.exception: Will be thrown for invalid indices.
member.returns: Returns a list of items.

member.name: P:Thermo.Chromeleon.Sdk.Interfaces.Instruments.IAuditTrailMessage.IsOverlapped
member.summary:
Whether the event was overlapped
This is a bit ambivalent. It can either indicate that the event refers to a future injection being prepared now, or it can indicate a preparation event for the current injection that was executed earlier.
It is possible to distinguish those by their location in the injection audit trail: A message referring to a future injection will be somewhere after the start of the current injection. A message referring to the current injection will be before the start of the current injection.
In an instrument audit trail, overlapped messages occur only once (at the time when they are issued).

member.name: P:Thermo.Chromeleon.Sdk.Interfaces.Instruments.Symbols.IDevice.DefaultGetProperty
member.summary:
Returns the default Property to get in an assignment from the Device.
If one of the Properties of a Device is the DefaultGetProperty it is allowed to assign the Device directly to another variable. E.g. "MyStateVar = Relay" is interpreted as "MyStateVar = Relay.State" if Relay.State is the DefaultGetProperty of the Relay Device. If no DefaultGetProperty is set the short form is not allowed.

member.name: P:Thermo.Chromeleon.Sdk.Interfaces.Instruments.Symbols.IDevice.DefaultSetProperty
member.summary:
Returns the default Property to set in an assignment to the Device.
If one of the Properties of a Device is the DefaultSetProperty it is allowed to assign a new value directly to the Device. E.g. "Relay = On" is interpreted as "Relay.State = On" if Relay.State is the DefaultSetProperty of the Relay Device. If no DefaultSetProperty is set the short form is not allowed.

member.name: P:Thermo.Chromeleon.Sdk.Interfaces.Instruments.Symbols.IParameter.ByName
member.summary:
If set to true, the parameter must be specified with its name if it is used in a parameter list. If set to false the parameter name can be omitted if all preceding parameters are specified.
Example: The parameter 'Timeout' of the Wait command specifies ByName=true; So, the following parameter list '1; Continue; 50' will not be valid. The correct parameter list will be '1; Continue; Timeout=50'.

An example for the reference parameter is the "Property" parameter on the "Log" system command. The "Property" parameter of the Log command then specifies the '.' separated path to the property which is referenced. Example: Log "ColumnOven.Temperature.Nominal".
Reference parameters can be used in Chromeleon symbols.

If one of the properties of a struct is the DefaultGetProperty, it is allowed to assign the struct directly to another variable. E.g. "Temperature = 25.0" is interpreted as "Temperature.Nominal = 25.0" if Temperature.Nominal is the DefaultSetProperty of the Temperature struct. If no DefaultSetProperty is set the short form is not allowed.

member.name: T:Thermo.Chromeleon.Sdk.Interfaces.RawData.Collections.IDataPointList
member.summary: This interface provides index-based access to some data points. The access is read-only. An implementation of this interface might directly contain a list of data points. Or it might only implement a filter-like operation (e.g. smoothing) on a different data points interface. The interface can be used to access the data points of 2D signals as well as the data points of spectra.

member.name: P:Thermo.Chromeleon.Sdk.Interfaces.RawData.Collections.IDataPointList.Item(System.Int32)
member.summary: Return the data point with the given zero-based index.
member.param: The zero-based index of the requested data point.
member.returns: A copy of the data point with the given zero-based index.

member.name: M:Thermo.Chromeleon.Sdk.Interfaces.RawData.Collections.IDataPointList.IndexAtOrBefore(System.Double)
member.summary:
Return the zero-based index of the data point at or before the given x-value. x might be e.g. the time of a signal. x is increased by a small epsilon (currently 1E-12) before the search to avoid rounding problems with floating point numbers.
Throw an exception if the x-value is less than the x-value of the first data point.
Most implementations (e.g. DataPointList, SignalReaderBaseWithPoints, NativeSignalReader, Spectrum and SelfContainedSpectrum) use a binary search. The time complexity of this function is in these cases therefore O(log(Count)).
member.param: The x-value whose index is searched.
member.returns: A valid zero-based data point index.

member.name: M:Thermo.Chromeleon.Sdk.Interfaces.RawData.Collections.IDataPointList.IndexAtOrAfter(System.Double)
member.summary:
Return the zero-based index of the data point at or after the given x-value. x might be e.g. the time of a signal. x is decreased by a small epsilon (currently 1E-12) before the search to avoid rounding problems with floating point numbers.
Throw an exception if the x-value is greater than the x-value of the last data point.
Most implementations (e.g. DataPointList, SignalReaderBaseWithPoints, NativeSignalReader, Spectrum and SelfContainedSpectrum) use a binary search. The time complexity of this function is in these cases therefore O(log(Count)).
member.param: The x-value whose index is searched.
member.returns: A valid zero-based data point index.

member.name: P:Thermo.Chromeleon.Sdk.Interfaces.RawData.ISignalMetadata.CreationVersion
member.summary: The Chromeleon version that created the signal. It might be null if the version is unknown. If it is not null then the fields "Major", "Minor", "Build" and possibly "Revision" are valid. "Build" contains the CM SR/SP number. "Revision" contains the CM build number iff the signal was created with CM 7.2 build 1214 or higher. The creation version is the Chromeleon version that created the encoded points. It is preserved during copy or backup + import (because these operations copy the binary file that contains the encoded points). Therefore the creation version is usually equal to the Chromeleon version that recorded the signal. The latter version is also available via the injection audit trail (precondition log).

member.name: M:Thermo.Chromeleon.Sdk.Interfaces.UserManagement.ILogon.DoLogon
member.summary: If user mode is enabled: Opens the logon dialog and tries to logon. The dialog stays open, if logon was not successful. There are two ways, how this function call ends: successful logon, or logon aborted (by the user). If user mode is disabled, a default logon will be done without opening the logon dialog.

member.name: M:Thermo.Chromeleon.Sdk.Interfaces.UserManagement.ILogon.DoLogoff(System.String)
member.summary: Logs off a logged on user. In order to guarantee the access check functionality it is mandatory that you do not have "local" data item references. Otherwise access checks for those data items may fail.
member.param: Additional information for the audit trail.

member.name: M:Thermo.Chromeleon.Sdk.Interfaces.UserManagement.ILogon.DoLogoff

member.name: M:Thermo.Chromeleon.Sdk.Interfaces.UserManagement.ILogon.DoSilentLogon(System.String,System.String,Thermo.Chromeleon.Sdk.Interfaces.UserManagement.IRole)
member.summary: Tries to logon the user with the specified name, password and role. If the user management is disabled, a default logon from the operating system will be created. In this scenario, the provided username and password will be ignored.
member.exception: Thrown if something goes wrong during the logon

member.name: M:Thermo.Chromeleon.Sdk.Interfaces.UserManagement.ILogon.CreateToken(System.String,System.String,Thermo.Chromeleon.Sdk.Interfaces.UserManagement.IRole)
member.summary: Creates a dedicated token for the provided login information. This method call authenticates the user based on the provided login information, but does not actually logon the user. In order to logon the user and perform a Chromeleon operation, the provided token should be used with a call to .
member.remarks: Please note this method will throw an exception if the provided login information is not correct (e.g. wrong password, invalid role etc.). In addition to the limitations which apply to the token, the generated tokens will be invalid, when you restart the Chromeleon services. In this case you have to call this method again to create new tokens.
member.returns: Logon token

member.name: M:Thermo.Chromeleon.Sdk.Interfaces.UserManagement.ILogon.PerformAuthenticatedAction(System.Action,System.String)
member.summary: Performs a Chromeleon operation based on the provided token. For the operation the corresponding user context (e.g. roles, access groups) linked to the provided token will be used. After the operation the original user context will be restored.
member.remarks: Throws an exception if the token is expired or unknown. In addition please note, the mentioned Chromeleon operation above is limited to data item operations (e.g. data item rename, copy, delete etc.). Instrument related operations are not supported to work with this token based authentication and will likely result in unspecified behavior.
member.param: The Chromeleon data item action to be performed.

member.name: M:Thermo.Chromeleon.Sdk.Interfaces.UserManagement.ILogon.DestroyToken(System.String)
member.summary: Tries to destroy the provided token. If the provided token does not exist, nothing will happen.
